title: The dominated-or-dominating pair degree-sum conjecture for supereulerian digraphs
statement:
Let $D$ be a strong digraph with $n$ vertices. A pair is **dominated or dominating** when it is a pair of dominated or dominating nonadjacent vertices of $D$ as specified in the source. A digraph is **supereulerian** if it contains a closed ditrail spanning all vertices, equivalently, a spanning eulerian subdigraph. **The dominated-or-dominating pair degree-sum conjecture.** If for any pair of dominated or dominating nonadjacent vertices $\{u,v\}$ of $D$, 

$$
d(u)+d(v)\geq 2n-3,
$$

then $D$ is supereulerian. This is presented as a possible generalization of the known degree-sum theorem for all nonadjacent pairs, and its resolution is not given in the supplied text.
source_name: Changchang Dong, Jixiang Meng and Juan Liu, “A new condition on dominated pair degree sum for a digraph to be supereulerian”, arXiv:2406.15841 (2024).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2406.15841

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of June 2024).
